headline: Navajo Nation Guided Tour Reservations
reservation: Access to Upper and Lower Antelope Canyon is strictly by authorized Navajo guide only; independent hiking is prohibited. Demand is extreme; reserve months in advance for peak sunbeam seasons. Check the Navajo Nation Parks & Recreation site for official closures and entry fees.

days.title: Sandstone Curves and Sculpted Walls

stops.name: Upper or Lower Antelope Canyon
stops.detail: Follow an authorized guide through the narrow slot canyon to see the wind-carved Navajo Sandstone.

stops.name: Glen Canyon Dam Overlook
stops.detail: View the massive concrete arch dam and the Colorado River from a designated rock viewpoint.

days.driving: Allow 15-20 minutes between Page and tour staging areas
days.note: Verify if your tour operates on Mountain Standard Time or Daylight Saving Time, as local zones vary.

days.title: Panoramic Overlooks and Deep Bends

stops.name: Horseshoe Bend
stops.detail: Walk the 1.5-mile round-trip path to see the Colorado River's 270-degree curve from the cliff edge.

stops.name: Lake Powell Wahweap Overlook
stops.detail: Gain a wide perspective of the reservoir and the surrounding desert mesas.

days.driving: Local transfers under 15 minutes; allow for parking queues
days.note: There is no shade at Horseshoe Bend; carry water even for this short walk.

days.title: Desert Shores and High Plateaus

stops.name: Lone Rock Beach
stops.detail: Visit the shoreline of Lake Powell to see the solitary monolithic rock rising from the water.

stops.name: Navajo Bridge
stops.detail: Walk the historic pedestrian bridge over Marble Canyon for views of the river far below.

days.driving: Allow 45 minutes for the drive toward Marble Canyon; conditions vary by wind
days.note: Check the Glen Canyon NRA site for current water levels and beach access.

intel.title: Controlled Lots
intel.text: Horseshoe Bend uses a city-managed paid parking system that often reaches capacity by midday. Canyon tours have dedicated staging lots; arrive 30 minutes early as required by operators.

intel.title: Navajo Land Coverage
intel.text: Cell service is consistent in the town of Page but can be non-existent inside the slot canyons and remote lake areas. Always keep a hard copy of your tour confirmation.

intel.title: Desert Distance
intel.text: Page is the primary hub for fuel and water; supplies become very sparse once you head toward Kanab or the Kaibab Plateau. Do not depart town with less than half a tank.

intel.title: Tour Duration
intel.text: Standard tours last approximately 90 minutes; however, weather-related flash flood warnings can cause immediate cancellations. Lighting for photography changes by the minute.

intel.title: Mobility and Gear
intel.text: Lower Antelope involves steep metal ladders and narrow squeezes; Upper is generally level but involves soft sand. Most operators prohibit backpacks and tripods inside the canyons.

plan.arrival: Fly into Page (PGA) or drive from Flagstaff; check in at your Page hotel or glamping site before your scheduled canyon check-in time.
plan.vehicle: Standard cars are fine for paved Page roads, but high-clearance vehicles are recommended for any off-pavement lake access points.
plan.goldenHour: Horseshoe Bend for sunset; be aware that the sun drops behind the cliffs earlier than the official sunset time.
